Marathon Petroleum dropped 0.37% today to close at $400.89, extending a sharp reversal from its peak earlier this week. The stock fell after climbing to $424.89 on September 18th, with today's decline reflecting dimmed optimism around oil prices and refining margins. Crude oil prices weakened on hopes for U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks and potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz—developments that would ease the supply constraints that have supported refiner profits in recent weeks. At the same time, the Trump administration is examining a possible diesel export ban, which adds regulatory uncertainty for a company heavily exposed to fuel exports and refining margins.

The broader context is one of genuine uncertainty about where energy markets head from here. Refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with solid fuel inventories, but Wall Street has publicly admitted it doesn't know the trajectory of oil prices given the geopolitical volatility. A diplomatic solution in Iran—which would increase global oil supply and reduce refining premiums—is precisely the kind of outcome that pressures refiner stocks, even if it brings broader economic stability.
